operation_tail.detail: ONSPD postcode currency is tied to the third Friday of the month before release; release date and postcode reference date are not conflated.
Current and terminated postcode status is based on monthly Royal Mail input and remains release-vintage specific.
Postcode currency, administrative/electoral geography currency and health geography currency are separate dates and are not represented as one universal snapshot.
Administrative, electoral and health area identities use GSS standard nine-character codes; names are not used as the sole join key.
Statutory area names are resolved through accompanying lookup files rather than inferred from code prefixes.
Seven-character, eight-character and single-space variable postcode formats are distinct representations of the same identity and are normalized explicitly.
DOINTR records the most recent introduction occurrence in YYYYMM format and is not treated as a daily timestamp.
A null DOTERM denotes a live postcode; a populated YYYYMM value denotes the most recent termination occurrence.
When Royal Mail reuses a postcode, old location and termination references are removed and the new location becomes the current identity; stale coordinates are rejected.
A reused postcode may initially receive an ONS-imputed grid reference before later AddressBase improvement, so current status alone is not sufficient for high positional confidence.
Areal data linked to terminated postcodes is refreshed before releases; terminated status does not imply historic geography fields are frozen.
Postcodes terminated before November 2000 can carry traditional-directory grid references with PQI 8 and are not promoted as precise current locations.
PQI 1 is within the matched building closest to the postcode mean; it still does not prove identity with a specific HMLR parcel.
PQI 2 is a Scotland-specific visual-inspection variant and is not applicable to the England shard.
PQI 3 is approximate within 50 metres and cannot support exact parcel-coordinate claims.
PQI 4 is a postcode-unit mean not snapped to a building and remains area-level evidence.
PQI 5 is imputed from surrounding postcode references and is treated as lower positional confidence.
PQI 6 is a postcode-sector mean, mainly for PO Boxes, and is excluded from parcel-level promotion.
PQI 8 represents a terminated postcode's last known ONS grid reference and remains review-only.
PQI 9 means no coordinates are available; no coordinate or parcel inference is written.
ONSPD provides one-metre grid references and derived latitude/longitude; these are alternative coordinate representations, not independent confirmations.
Latitude and longitude are calculated from easting/northing transformations and are not treated as separately surveyed observations.
Newly introduced postcodes may initially be imputed and later replaced by AddressBase survey-derived references.
Demolition and new-build can change the address set and move the postcode centroid, requiring current-release validation.
A change from imputed to surveyed coordinates can change geography assignments; older assignments are not carried forward blindly.
A postcode spanning multiple administrative areas is assigned to one area using a single mean reference, so address-level allocation can be imprecise.
ONS identifies imputation as a source of wrong area assignments; such records are not elevated to exact parcel confidence.
Very recent postcodes introduced after the monthly update may be absent from the current directory; absence is not converted into a negative coverage result.
ONS gives no warranty of ONSPD accuracy or comprehensiveness, so binary, lifecycle and row-level validation remain mandatory.
Identified errors and omissions are incorporated into a subsequent ONSPD release; corrections are not silently backfilled into older snapshots.
ONS recommends the multi-CSV distribution when spreadsheet limits cannot preserve the full standard file.
Spreadsheet opening is not accepted as completeness proof for the large ONSPD dataset.
Non-geographic and PO Box postcodes may point to a Royal Mail sorting office rather than the served user address.
Royal Mail postcode reorganisations can replace earlier districts or units; joins require current normalized postcode identity.
The official archive may retain an outer r1 name while all-premises postcode members must be inner r2; archive acceptance checks both layers.
Each of the 121 all-premises members must match its postcode-area filename and internal postcode-area values.
The separate residential r1 member set is not substituted for the all-premises r2 join required by this slot.
All required official percentage fields must be numeric and within 0 to 100 before a candidate can reach 3/4 accuracy.
Fresh canonical evidence shows no live owner and no active or long PENDING task; no duplicate task, commit chain or runner was created.
Forty official positional-quality, reuse, data-quality, parser and archive-member controls were published line by line; candidate counts remain unchanged pending strict r2 bytes.
